item.title: [SwiftHFR] Flag writes: name the failed session check, offer « Réessayer » when nothing left (#1056)
item.body:
Refs #1056 (what is left: (1) the cause on the operator's account, which this PR makes visible, see "Device check"; (2) the issue's acceptance criteria 1 and 2, a real swipe removal on `user2` and a test on the captured non-valid answer: the Mac probe was read-only and its answer was `valid`, so there is no non-valid answer to capture yet; (3) follow-up: split the « Réseau indisponible » text by `NetworkError` as `PollMessages.network` does, Fable detail 2)
Claim: mac/M1
Author model: opus-5.5 (mac/M1)
Reviewer model: fable-5.1 (mac/M1-r1078-fable: APPROVE on d089c280, the head)

## Problem
A swipe-left removal in Favoris showed « Session non confirmée : rien n'a été envoyé. Reconnectez-vous puis réessayez. » on a session whose lists load. Every non-valid result of the LOT-044 session check (`SessionHealth`: 2 `expired` reasons and 3 `unconfirmed` ones) mapped to that **one** text. So the screenshot cannot tell which check failed, and « Reconnectez-vous » is wrong advice when the check merely proved nothing.

## What the Mac showed (2026-11-17, `dev-swift` 1df2121a, capture account user2 only, read-only)
- A fresh user2 session (logged in through `tooling/fixtures/flows.py`), run through `SessionRefreshFlow.refresh` (what `TopicFlagFlow.confirm` calls): **`valid`**.
- The probe request by hand (`/user/editprofil.php`, `config` + `page`, no redirect followed): **200, served at exactly the requested URL**, no `Location`, `Set-Cookie` present, not a `.hop`, the profile page parses, and the token is present.
- So HFR's profile page and the rules of `accountToken` hold. The non-valid answer on the operator's device comes from **the app-side state of that account's session**. Leads, not proven:
  - the account came from the legacy import, which keeps each cookie's own domain (`KeychainLegacyAccountSource.swift:89`), so the jar may hold two `md_user` and `userKey` takes the first non-empty one (`.unconfirmed(.identityNotConfirmed)`);
  - a login generation or identity change while the check ran (`.unconfirmed(.sessionChanged)`);
  - or a real `.expired`.

  The lists and the flag writer share one `HFRSession` (`AppEnvironment.swift:44, 58`), so a stale copy is ruled out.

## Change
- `TopicFlagActions.session(_:)`: each case and reason has its own text, and every one keeps « rien n'a été envoyé ».
  - Only `.expired` says « Reconnectez-vous »: « Session expirée … » and « HFR refuse les identifiants de ce compte … ».
  - `.unconfirmed` says « Session non vérifiée (page de profil inattendue | identité non confirmée par HFR) … Réessayez dans quelques instants. »
  - `.sessionChanged`: « Le compte connecté a changé pendant la vérification … Réessayez. »
- `TopicFlagOutcome.retryable`: a write refused by an `.unconfirmed` check, or by the network before it left, offers « Réessayer » in the list's alert. The row is captured when the alert is built, because the alert clears its state before a button runs (LOT-087). A write that may have left (`.unconfirmed` answer), an expired session, a refusal or a missing token are never offered again.
- The health case is logged (`os.Logger`, subsystem `SwiftHFR`, category `session`, case and reason only, no cookie, no token).
- Polls already split their texts (`PollMessages.swift`). MP deletion and the group roster do not map `sessionNotConfirmed` in the app today, so nothing changes there.

Why no wider: no change to the engine's check. Its rules hold on a live session, and the cause on the device is not yet known.

## Tests (`TopicRowActionsTests`)
- `theSessionMessagesTellAnExpiredSessionFromAnUnconfirmedCheck`: « Reconnectez-vous » only for `expired`, « Réessayez » for `unconfirmed`, « rien n'a été envoyé » in all, five distinct texts.
- `anUnconfirmedSessionCheckOffersARetryThatSendsAgain`: the retry state is set, the retry sends again and removes the row, and dismissing clears it.
- `onlyANothingSentFailureThatMayPassOffersARetry` (4 cases): no retry after a possibly-sent write, an expired session, a refusal or a missing token.
- Mutations, each failing `anUnconfirmedSessionCheckOffersARetryThatSendsAgain:286`:
  - A: never retryable;
  - B: the old single message.
- Mac, iPhone 18 Pro simulator, iOS 27.0: `TopicRowActionsTests`, `MarkUnreadTests`, `FavoriteActionHandlerTests` 37/37; whole `SwiftHFRTests` 1,917 green.

## Device check (operator)
Swipe-remove a favourite on your account:
- if it works, nothing more is needed;
- if it fails, **the alert now names the check** (expired / page inattendue / identité non confirmée / compte changé), and Console.app (subsystem `SwiftHFR`, category `session`) shows the case. Post that text on #1056: it tells which lead is the cause.

« Réessayer » must resend once and remove the row.

This is a state-changing flow: **cloud/orch merges it** (AGENTS.md §8), after the Fable review.

comments.body:
**Adversarial review (fable-5.2, mac/M1-r1078-fable, d089c280) : APPROVE** — tête d089c280

**Revue adversariale (Fable 5.1) : APPROUVÉ** — tête d089c280

Strictness checks on the state-changing flow, all held:
- `TopicFlagFlow.exchange` throws `.network` only before the request leaves (`Task.isCancelled`, `invalidRequest` pre-flight); anything after is `.unconfirmed(.transport)`, and `isRetryable` maps `.unconfirmed` and `.sessionNotConfirmed(.expired)` to `.failed`. « Réessayer » can never resend a write that may have left.
- Double send: `removingFlags` guard; the retry runs after the first call's `defer`, the alert is modal, one tap. The session is per account (`AccountsModel.sessions[id]`, screens rebuilt on `currentSessionGeneration`), so a retry cannot cross accounts; a stale row only resends an idempotent `delflag` for its `TopicID`.
- Every `TopicFlagOutcome` switch updated (4 sites, compiler-checked by the build). Log line: enum case only. Lines ≤ 140, `session(_:)` 6 branches.

Findings:
1. **Low** — PR body, "what is left": the issue's acceptance criteria 1–2 (a real swipe removal on `user2` on the Mac, a test on the captured non-valid answer) were not done (read-only probe only). `Refs #1056` is right; list both explicitly so #1056 keeps them.
2. **Detail** — `App/SwiftHFR/Navigation/TopicFlagActions.swift:119-120`: « Réseau indisponible : rien n'a été envoyé. » now sits under « Réessayer » for every `NetworkError`, including a 5xx of the probe GET and `.cancelled`; misleading for those. Split as `PollMessages.network` does (pre-existing text, follow-up acceptable).
3. **Detail** — straight apostrophes here vs typographic ones in `PollMessages.swift`; pre-existing in this file.
4. **Detail** — reader add-favourite and mark unread fold `.retryable` into the failed path (message names the check, no retry button); consistent with the issue's scope 4 since the menu can simply be reused.

**Vérifié** — worktree at d089c280 (removed), iPhone 18 Pro simulator 3C7DA65A, iOS 27.0: `TopicRowActionsTests` + `MarkUnreadTests` + `FavoriteActionHandlerTests` 49/49 passed. Mutation of my own (`.unconfirmed` made retryable in `isRetryable`): `onlyANothingSentFailureThatMayPassOffersARetry` fails on the `.unconfirmed` argument only, then reverted. Line-length check by awk on every changed file (none > 140); `swiftlint` binary not available locally. Read `TopicFlagFlow`, `SessionRefreshFlow`, `SessionHealth`, `TopicFlagError`, `NetworkError`, `AppEnvironment`, `AccountsModel`, `PollMessages`, `MPThreadDeletion` (not wired in the app: PR claim holds). DerivedData deleted, simulator shut down.

1. **Discovery**: `@Test` in an extension of the suite struct is discovered and run. Shown by a Linux probe (below); the repository already does this in `App/SwiftHFRTests/Reader/TopicReaderModelTests.swift:253`.
2. **Isolation**: extension members inherit the type's `@MainActor`. In the probe, a synchronous extension test passes `MainActor.assertIsolated()` and builds a `@MainActor` model without `await`, in language mode 6.
3. **Access**: the extension calls the struct's `private` `favoritesList` and `titles`; same-file extension access compiles in the probe (private sync and async helpers called from the extension).
4. **Tests unchanged**: 18 `@Test` at both heads, identical name lists (same hash), and the diff has no deleted or modified line, so no body, argument list or name changed.
5. **Lint**: `swiftlint lint --strict` on the file: 0 violations at f29cf716; at d089c280 it reproduces `type_body_length` (268 > 250), so the commit fixes what it claims.

**Verified** (actually run)
- Fresh worktree at f29cf716; `git diff d089c280..f29cf716`, plain and with `-w --ignore-blank-lines`.
- `swiftlint lint --strict` on the file at both heads.
- Probe package, Swift 6.2.4 on Linux, language mode 6: a `@MainActor` struct with private helpers and a same-file extension holding a sync, an async and a parameterized `@Test`; `swift test`: 4 tests in 1 suite passed.
- Not run: the app test target itself (it cannot build on Linux); the macOS CI run remains the arbiter for it.
